about: Editorial decisions applied by tools/guide/import-blurbs.py to the source snapshot named by 'source'. A decision names its record by source line; 'platform' and 'title' are that record's public identity and must match it, so an edited or reordered source cannot apply a decision to another game. Excluded records have no public identity and are guarded by the snapshot hash. 'hook' and 'controls' replace the published text; 'dropFlags'/'addFlags' adjust published flags; 'exclude' leaves the record out; 'work' assigns a justified shared work id. The authored source is never changed.

decisions.title: Soulcalibur III - Arcade Edition Deluxe (v1.21 Hack)
decisions.hook: A fan build of Soulcalibur III from TopazTK's project to port the Arcade Edition to PS2. CDRomance's v1.21 notes list playable Hilde, Inferno, Colossus, Charade and others, plus new costumes, reshuffled Tales of Souls opponents and a Soul Edge (Complete) weapon set. The project's own v1.20 notes left out true Arcade Edition movesets and costumes because they broke the game, so how much arcade balance this build has is unverified.

decisions.title: Marvel - Ultimate Alliance 2
decisions.hook: This is n-Space's PS2 version of the Civil War sequel, not the PS3/360 game. Pick Pro or Anti-Registration, build four-hero teams, and pair heroes for fusion attacks. Levels, balance and powers differ from PS3/360, and the roster adds Psylocke, Cyclops and Blade. User reviews cite long loads and slowdown.
decisions.reason: Described byte checks of the curator's private copy and its dump status; removed, with the dump-status flag.

decisions.title: Muramasa Rebirth
decisions.hook: Vanillaware's hand-painted 2D action RPG: equip three blades and switch among them, because blocking and Secret Arts drain each blade's Soul Power until it breaks, then it regenerates in its sheath. Forging all 108 blades, cooking and two protagonists add long-term pull. Rebirth is the Vita version with Aksys's redone localisation. Critics found the combat fun but shallow.
decisions.reason: Described the contents of the curator's private copy; removed.

decisions.title: Call of Duty Black Ops - Declassified
decisions.hook: Nihilistic's Vita-exclusive Call of Duty: about a dozen short Operations missions, plus Time Trials and Hostiles wave survival. Pocket Gamer said a seasoned player could finish the story in around 45 minutes, with difficulty spikes from hostages and timers, and the narrative is disjointed. Campaign XP does not carry into online multiplayer. Thin, poorly reviewed and not systemic; worth trying only as a curiosity.
decisions.reason: Refers to the curator's own library contents; removed.

decisions.title: Castlevania - The Dracula X Chronicles
decisions.hook: Three strong reasons to play this: a 2.5D Rondo of Blood remake, the original Rondo, and Symphony of the Night. The latter two must be unlocked inside the remake. Rondo offers branching stages, rescued characters and demanding boss patterns; Symphony supplies the exploratory equipment-and-ability game. Richter's committed movement is deliberately old-school, while Maria's double jump makes a friendlier alternative. Immediate action and route discovery, not a long JRPG introduction.
decisions.reason: Refers to the curator's own library contents; removed.

decisions.title: Dynasty Warriors
decisions.hook: The 1997 original is a one-on-one 3D weapon fighter, not the army-clearing Musou formula that began with Dynasty Warriors 2. Three Kingdoms officers meet in individual duels, so this fits a quick fighting-game session rather than a strategy or territory-management mood. An interesting prehistory of the series; do not pick it expecting a miniature version of the PS2 battlefield games.
decisions.reason: Personal taste framing addressed to the curator; removed so the sentence stands for any reader.

decisions.title: Anguna - Warriors of Virtue
decisions.hook: Nathan Tolbert's compact, top-down Zelda-like homebrew, with Chris Hildenbrand's art. Explore an overworld and dungeons, find hidden rooms and power-ups, and add a bow, bear traps, dynamite, a lantern and magic boots to the sword. A low-commitment exploration snack rather than a deep character-building sandbox. Written about the No-Intro v0.95 build; the creator's current release page mixes five- and six-dungeon descriptions, so do not infer later-edition extras from it.
decisions.reason: Spoke about the curator's particular file; matching ignores version tags, so the claim is anchored to the version it describes.

decisions.title: JSRF - Jet Set Radio Future
decisions.hook: Smilebit turns futuristic Tokyo into a skating playground: chain grinds and wall rides, hunt hidden graffiti souls, and tag rival territory without the original game's constant stage timer. Boosts consume spray cans, while police encounters punctuate the exploration. Built for movement mastery and finding your own routes rather than gear-building or stealth simulation. A working Android launch setup has not been verified.
decisions.reason: Taste-fit framing, the curator's scraping state and a device-specific flag; the gameplay description is kept.

decisions.title: Chaotix Complete (Hack)
decisions.hook: An experimental 32X hack labelled Chaotix Complete v0.1. The ROM header confirms that title and version, and the release archive credits AdamKempenich, but it contains no changelog; public searches did not establish its exact alterations. Treat this as a curiosity to sample, not a verified definitive edition or a promised fix for the original's mechanics. Patch completeness, save behaviour and compatibility have not been playtested.
decisions.reason: Referred to the archive the curator received; restated as the release archive.

decisions.title: Harmful Park (v1.1 Translation)
decisions.hook: Sky Think System's colourful horizontal shooter hides a real scoring game beneath its theme-park gags. Switch freely among potato shots, ice-cream lasers, pies and homing jelly; each has its own bomb. Six stages reward lining up multi-kills and collecting gems without dropping the chain, with a separate Score Attack stage for repeat runs. A good change of pace from Cave's bullet curtains without abandoning route mastery. Hilltop's English patch translates the cutscenes and nearly all background text; the patch archive labels it v1.1.
decisions.reason: Referred to the archive the curator received; restated as the patch archive.
